text.p: Heliopolis Housing and Development deputy chairman denied on Wednesday market rumours that the realty firm would issue a 10-to-one share split in February or that it would give away free shares.
"The nominal value of our shares is currently five pounds and that is the minimum it can go by law," Abdel Baqi Mubarak, who is also the firm's financial director, told Reuters.

Some brokers trading at the Cairo stock exchange had said the firm would split its shares next month. Others said they heard that Heliopolis Housing would give a free share for every two as part of its dividend.
"We are not thinking right now about giving away any free shares or splitting shares. We cannot currently fund such an operation," Mubarak said. "Any proposals we get are still being considered."
Heliopolis Housing announced that it would give a 10.90 pound dividend for the 1995/6 financial year. The firm is one of the most popular and influential on the stock market.
